issues.legal_issue: A usufructuary mortgage debt is eligible for adjustment even when the creditor cannot proceed personally against the debtor.
material_facts: The debt was secured by a mortgage with possession over agricultural land belonging to displaced persons.
The mortgagees were placed in possession of land allotted in India in substitution for land they had possessed in Pakistan.
One applicant held the equity of redemption, although the mortgagees’ personal right to recover the debt from that applicant was disputed.
issues.conclusion: A usufructuary mortgage is a debt eligible for adjustment regardless of whether the creditor can proceed personally against the debtor.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 2(6), 2(9) and 16(4) of the Displaced Persons (Debts Adjustment) Act, 1951, read together, bring usufructuary mortgage debts within the Act; personal enforceability is immaterial. The Court relied on Lahori Lal v. Kasturi Lal and Rajkumari Kaushalya Devi v. Bawa Pritam Singh, and distinguished Lachhman Singh v. Natha Singh and Manubhai Mahijibhai Patel v. Trikamlal Laxmidas as involving different statutory definitions.

rule.if: displaced_person_debt_adjustment_proceeding and agricultural_land_secures_debt and mortgage_is_with_possession and mortgagee_received_replacement_land

predicates.displaced_person_debt_adjustment_proceed: A debtor seeks adjustment of a debt in a proceeding for adjusting debts owed by displaced persons.
predicates.agricultural_land_secures_debt: Agricultural land belonging to a displaced person secures the debt.
predicates.mortgage_is_with_possession: The mortgage gives the creditor possession of the secured land.
predicates.mortgagee_received_replacement_land: The creditor received replacement land in lieu of the land over which the creditor had possession.

issues.definition: When a displaced-person debt-adjustment proceeding concerns a debt secured by agricultural land under a mortgage with possession and the creditor received replacement land, the debt qualifies for adjustment as a usufructuary mortgage debt.

issues.legal_issue: A debtor may apply to a tribunal to adjust a secured mortgage debt without waiting for a redemption suit.
material_facts: The debtors applied to the tribunal for adjustment of the mortgage debt.
The debt was secured by a mortgage with possession over agricultural land, and the applicants sought the adjustment available for that kind of secured debt.
The creditors contended that adjustment could occur only in a suit for redemption brought by the creditor.
issues.conclusion: A debtor may apply under the Act for adjustment of a mortgage debt; a creditor’s redemption suit is not required.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 5(1) and 16(4) of the Displaced Persons (Debts Adjustment) Act, 1951, allow a debtor to apply for adjustment of debts, including a secured debt covered by section 16(4).

predicates.displaced_person_debt_adjustment_proceed: A debtor seeks adjustment of a debt in a proceeding for adjusting debts owed by displaced persons.
predicates.debtor_applies_for_adjustment: The debtor files an application asking the tribunal to adjust the debt.
predicates.debt_is_secured_by_qualifying_mortgage: The debt is secured by a mortgage with possession over agricultural land of a displaced person, and the creditor received replacement land.

issues.definition: When a debtor applies in a displaced-person debt-adjustment proceeding and the debt is secured by the described mortgage, the debtor may seek adjustment by application.

issues.legal_issue: The relative value of land for reducing a mortgage debt may be determined through standard-acre equivalents that account for the land’s characteristics and yield rather than market value alone.
material_facts: The tribunal compared land left behind with land allotted through a standard-acre measure.
The rehabilitation rules and instructions took account of the income yield and nature of the land, including whether it was irrigated or rain-fed, when determining standard acres.
Market value in the sense of the price a willing purchaser would pay for the land left behind had not been ascertained.
issues.conclusion: Using standard-acre equivalents calculated under the rehabilitation rules was a proper way to reflect the relative value of the land for reducing the debt; market value alone was not required.
issues.legal_principle: The proviso to section 16(4) of the Displaced Persons (Debts Adjustment) Act, 1951, requires a proportionate reduction based on the value of the relevant lands. The Court held that the rules and instructions for computing standard acres reflected value by accounting for land yield and characteristics.

predicates.displaced_person_debt_adjustment_proceed: A debt is being adjusted in a proceeding for adjusting debts owed by displaced persons.
predicates.land_value_is_computed_through_standard_: The relevant lands are compared using standard-acre equivalents.
predicates.standard_acre_computation_accounts_for_l: The standard-acre computation accounts for the land’s yield or characteristics, such as its irrigation or cultivation conditions.

issues.definition: When a debt-adjustment proceeding compares lands using standard-acre equivalents that reflect yield or land characteristics, those equivalents may measure relative land value for reducing the debt.
